tagline.text: Mindanao's first SM mall, now bigger with a new wing, a shopping hub in Ecoland

location.label: Location
location.text: Quimpo Blvd corner Eco West Drive, Ecoland area, Matina, Davao City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (indoor mall; getting around is easiest in the March–May dry season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~2,000 (per person, meals, transport and light shopping)

children.text: SM City Davao opened on November 17, 2001 as the first SM mall in Mindanao, and locals more often call it SM Ecoland. With the new wing that soft-opened in July 2025 on top of the main mall and the Annex, it has grown even larger and works well for shopping, dining, movies and a rainy-day break in Davao City.

SM City Davao is an indoor shopping mall at the corner of Quimpo Boulevard and Eco West Drive in Matina, Davao City. It is developed and managed by SM Prime Holdings and opened on November 17, 2001, as the first SM mall in the Mindanao region. Wikipedia gives the site as about 13.2 hectares. SM's official page lists the address as Quimpo Blvd corner Tulip and Ecoland Drive in the Ecoland subdivision, which is why many locals skip the mall name and say SM Ecoland. Telling a taxi or Grab driver "SM Ecoland" is the quickest way to be understood.

The complex has three parts. First is the Main Mall built in 2001, a three-level building anchored by SM Store and SM Supermarket, with cinemas and dining spread across the floors. The Annex, which opened on March 9, 2012, has shops on its lower two levels and BPO office space above. The newest is the Expansion Wing, which soft-opened on July 29, 2025. According to SM's official news, it is a seven-level building with more than 100,000 square meters of floor area, and its upper floors are planned to house the first National University campus in Mindanao. Wikipedia puts the whole mall at about 120,000 square meters as of 2026 while other sources give larger figures, so floor-area numbers differ by source; just think of it as a very large mall.

For travelers, this mall is less a sightseeing attraction than the center of everyday life in Davao. In air-conditioned comfort you can change money, buy a SIM card, visit a pharmacy, shop at the supermarket, see a movie and eat with kids, all in one stop. Families staying in Davao for a month or longer often use it for their first grocery run and household shopping. It is also a handy fallback when a sudden squall wipes out your plans. Other big malls in the city include SM Lanang Premier in Lanang and Abreeza Mall, but the one closest to the city center is this mall in Ecoland.

There are also a few moments in its history worth knowing. On the night of September 16, 2013 (Wikipedia gives the 17th), during two cinema bombings in Davao, an explosion also occurred in Cinema 1 at this mall, and no serious casualties were reported. Today every entrance has a security check, so please cooperate when asked to open your bag, even if it is a bit inconvenient. During the December 2019 Davao del Sur earthquake, Wikipedia says the upper part of the Annex and some ceilings outside the mall were damaged, with no deaths or injuries reported (we could not confirm this from another source).

Opened on November 17, 2001, this was the first mall SM Group built in Mindanao. After more than 20 years as a meeting spot for Davao residents, telling a local friend "let's meet at SM in Ecoland" is enough. It is also interesting to compare the older layout of the Main Mall with the modern feel of the new wing on the same day.

Reports say the wing, which soft-opened on July 29, includes Nanyang's first Mindanao restaurant serving Singaporean cuisine, the Asian-fusion Brique Modern Kitchen and the local cafe Good One Cafe & Yogurt. The Danish lifestyle store Flying Tiger has also opened on the 2nd level. Tenants keep changing, so check the in-mall directory or the SM app for the latest list.

At SM Store, the Main Mall's anchor, you can buy clothing, accessories and household goods in one place, and at SM Supermarket you can pick up gift foods such as Philippine snacks, mangoes, coconut products, and Davao specialties like processed durian products and coffee. If you need Korean instant noodles or seasonings, a quick walk down the supermarket aisles usually turns them up.

The Main Mall has SM Cinema, and Wikipedia lists six digital cinemas. SM's official news says the theaters are being upgraded with the expansion to include two private cinemas and two Director's Club cinemas. With leather seating and food service, these premium cinemas are a good way to spend the hot part of the day. Check the SM Cinema app for showtimes and prices.

The choices run from food courts and fast food to cafes, Filipino restaurants, and Japanese and Korean outlets. Philippine chains such as Jollibee and Mang Inasal are here, and new restaurants are reported to keep opening in the new wing. Lunch and dinner hours get crowded, so it is better to arrive a little early.

The Annex has a Cyberzone area selling electronics and IT products. You can also find money changers, bank ATMs, telecom shops and pharmacies inside the mall, which is handy for buying a SIM card or withdrawing cash. Wikipedia notes that a Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) passport office opened on the third level of the Main Mall in 2012, but check the latest announcements to see whether it is still operating.

Wide corridors, air conditioning, restrooms, nursing rooms and children's stores make it easy to visit with kids. SM's official page says free Wi-Fi is available inside the mall. After an outdoor day in the heat, it is an easy place to stop and rest.
Arrive when the mall opens at
, pass the entrance security check and scan the Main Mall directory on the first floor to see what is on each level. Fewer people are around, so it is a good time to browse.
Choose gifts such as snacks, mangoes, coffee and processed durian products at SM Supermarket, and take care of money changing and telecom shops at this time.

Have lunch at the food court or at one of the new restaurants in the new wing. Lines at places like Nanyang or Brique Modern Kitchen can get long at lunchtime, so I recommend heading over around 11:30.
Look around the new shops on the 2nd level of the new wing, and walk between the Main Mall and the new wing by stairs or escalator to get a feel for the layout.
Finish with a movie or a rest at a cafe.
The mall is strongly air-conditioned, so a light jacket helps.

items.title: Fitting it into a full day in Davao City
items.subtitle: Rest at the mall after a morning of sightseeing

children.text: Start with city-center sights such as a church or a park in downtown Davao.
Take a taxi or Grab to SM Ecoland, have lunch and escape the heat.
Finish your grocery shopping and money changing, then head back to your lodging before the evening traffic.
A nonstop flight from Manila (NAIA) to Francisco Bangoy International Airport, Davao (DVO) takes about
2 hours 10 minutes
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check before booking.
From the airport to the mall by taxi or Grab takes about
20–40 minutes
(about 13.7 km). Wikivoyage (as of 2023) puts a metered taxi to downtown at ₱200–300 and another guide at ₱200–350, and Grab reportedly adds about ₱25 on top of the meter, so budget
or so, which varies with traffic and how you hail the ride, so check the app quote.

items.title: Taxi or Grab from the city

children.text: From central Davao, a short Grab or taxi ride can cost roughly
. This is an estimate from a 2026 blog, so check the quote in the app.
Enter SM City Davao or SM Ecoland as your destination. Be careful not to confuse it with SM Lanang Premier in Lanang.
Jeepneys and city buses heading along Quimpo Boulevard toward Ecoland pass in front of the mall. The base fare is cited at around
, but routes and fares change, so confirm locally.
A transport terminal that stood beside the mall was reported to have been demolished for the new wing, so do not trust stop locations in older blogs.
Some guides say the Ecoland bus terminal is right nearby, which is convenient for intercity bus travelers, but check its current location locally.

It is an indoor mall, so you can go any time of year. Davao is relatively out of the typhoon belt and its dry and wet seasons are not sharply divided, but sudden afternoon squalls are common, so the mall serves as a refuge between plans.

Time of day and day of week matter more for crowds. Weekday daytime is quiet, while Friday evenings, weekends and payday weeks are busy. At year-end, opening hours are extended and crowds are at their largest.

Around the mall in Matina and Ecoland there are many budget and mid-range hotels, serviced residences and apartments, and many families staying for a month or more live here. You can walk to the mall or take a short taxi ride, and some places offer shuttles or free Wi-Fi, so check before booking.

Meals mainly mean the food court and restaurants inside the mall. Outside, local eateries and street food line Quimpo Boulevard, and Davao's signature fruits such as durian, pomelo and marang are cheaper at the city markets. Inside the mall, choosing long-established chains is the safer bet.
There are bag checks at every entrance, so leave large bags and luggage behind and travel light.
Tell your Grab or taxi driver "SM City Davao" or "SM Ecoland," and confirm it is not the Lanang branch.
Weekday daytime is less crowded, while Friday evenings and weekends are busy.
Tenants in the new wing are still growing, so check the SM website or the in-mall directory for the current list.
Cinemas are strongly air-conditioned, so bring a light jacket.
Money changers inside the mall offer different rates, so compare two or three.
Year-end and holiday opening hours differ from usual, so check SM's official page before you go.
When a squall hits, jeepneys and taxis are hard to catch, so it is better to book a Grab in advance.
Every entrance has a security check, so please cooperate, and watch for pickpockets and lost phones on crowded days.
Keep your belongings, especially your phone and wallet, in a front pocket or inside your bag.
For Grab, check the fare in the app, and for taxis hailed on the street, make sure the meter is on.

Opening hours vary by day and holiday. SM's official site lists 10:00–21:00 Monday to Thursday and Sunday, and 10:00–22:00 Friday and Saturday. However, in late March 2026 news reported that SM and other Davao malls would shorten weekday hours to 11:00–21:00 to save electricity, so check locally before you go.
After the soft opening, construction and tenant openings in the new wing continue, so some areas may be closed off.
Quimpo Boulevard outside the mall is congested, so use the footbridge or crossing signals.
The city center is about
15–25 minutes
from the mall by car, and you can easily combine other Davao sights into the same day.

15–20 minutes
from the mall by taxi.
A mall of the same chain in the Lanang district near the airport, in the north of Davao City, unlike the Ecoland branch.
